system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING

PHYSICS CHECK — Governing relation: Fick's law of diffusion for electrolyte loss and Arrhenius equation for temperature-dependent evaporation. Verify that the new seal material reduces electrolyte permeation rate by at least 50% at 65°C compared to the baseline, while maintaining equivalent ionic conductivity within 5% of original electrolyte. The seal must also withstand mechanical cycling during thermal expansion/contraction without cracking.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components: 1) Fluorinated elastomer (FKM) gaskets with 1.5 mm thickness (USER CONSTRAINT: height limit), 2) Aluminum oxide ceramic coating (50 nm) on current collectors to reduce localized heating, 3) Modified electrolyte with 10% higher boiling point solvent (e.g., propylene carbonate), 4) Integrated temperature sensor array at cell interfaces. Procedure: Replace existing EPDM seals with FKM seals during module assembly; apply ceramic coating via atomic layer deposition; modify electrolyte formulation during cell filling.

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — Implementation burden is moderate (requires new material sourcing and process adjustment) compared to standard EPDM seals. Cost increases by ~15% per module but eliminates need for more complex thermal management systems. Maintenance remains identical to standard practice; no additional operational steps required.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Accelerated aging test with 20 modules, half with new design, half with baseline. Cycle between 25°C and 85°C (65°C average) at 2.7V for 2000 hours (equivalent to 10 years at 65°C), with cold-crank pulse tests every 500 hours. Instruments: ESR meter, capacitance tester, environmental chamber. Pass/fail: ESR increase <20% and capacitance loss <10% after test. Duration: 2000 hours continuous. Falsification: Any module exceeding ESR increase >20% or capacitance loss >10% fails the test.
